headline: Sterling is near 1.3210 against the dollar early on Thursday in Dubai, after falling 0.42% on Wednesday as the dollar index rose to about 102.2, near its strongest since spring 2025. The Fed minutes, US bond yields near 5.3% and oil near $102 (about £77) support the dollar, and a Fed governor, the Bank of England Governor and US weekly jobless claims are the scheduled tests this afternoon.

drivers.title: Fed rate expectations
drivers.text: The minutes of the Fed's September meeting, released on 7 October, record that all participants supported the rise to a range of 3.75% to 4% and that most thought another rise would likely be appropriate by the end of the year. Futures put the chance of a quarter point rise on 28 October at 19.4%, down from about 38% a week earlier, and the chance of a rise by the December meeting at 83%, Reuters reported on 7 October. Soft US figures, including 29,000 jobs added in September against 90,000 expected, lie behind the lower October figure.

drivers.title: US bond yields
drivers.text: The US ten-year yield touched 5.35% on Thursday 8 October, its highest since 2002, then fell back to about 5.24%, its lowest since Monday, after the President ruled out an early strike on Iran, Trading Economics and NBC News reported. A sale of $22 billion (about £16.6 billion) of 30-year bonds the same evening drew ordinary demand at a yield of 5.618%. Higher US yields draw money into the dollar.

drivers.title: Oil and the Middle East
drivers.text: President Trump said on Thursday 8 October that the United States will not attack Iran at any time before the midterm elections on 3 November and that productive discussions with Tehran are under way, while the naval blockade stays in place, the Tribune and CBS News reported. Brent crude, which had reached $105.92 (about £80) a barrel after The Atlantic reported that the White House had asked the Pentagon for strike options, eased to about $104 (about £79), still more than 3% higher on the day, NBC News and Trading Economics reported. Tanker attacks in the Gulf and a tropical storm that has shut in about a quarter of US Gulf of Mexico output keep oil supported.

drivers.title: The euro and European bonds
drivers.text: The euro fell 0.53% to 1.1198 against the dollar on Wednesday 7 October, close to the 17-month low it reached on Monday, as the French ten-year yield jumped 11.9 basis points to 4.87% on worries about the budget deficit, Reuters reported. A weaker euro lifts the dollar index and tends to pull GBP/USD down with it, although sterling reached its highest against the euro since June 2025.

drivers.title: The UK side
drivers.text: The Bank of England held Bank Rate at 3.75% on 17 September, with three of the nine members voting for a rise, and its next decision is on 5 November. Markets price more than 100 basis points of further tightening by the end of next year, and Catherine Mann of the Bank has warned that inflation could reach 4% around the turn of the year, Trading Economics reported on 7 October. The Governor, Andrew Bailey, speaks on Thursday at 16:15 Dubai.

lower: Further talk from Fed policymakers of another rate rise by the end of the year, after Governor Waller backed more rises on Thursday, which supports the dollar.
Oil rising again on further attacks on tankers and on Saudi Arabia, or on a breakdown in the talks between the US and Iran, which adds to US inflation worries and tends to lift the dollar.
US consumer sentiment on Friday coming in above the 47.5 forecast, or inflation expectations rising from 4.6%, which would make Fed rises more likely.
Further selling of French bonds over the budget, which would weaken the euro and lift the dollar against every currency.
higher: Oil falling as Gulf exports recover and the faster release of oil stocks reaches the market, which eases US inflation worries and weakens the dollar.
Bank of England policymakers signalling a rate rise on 5 November, which would lift the pound; the Governor gave no such signal on Thursday.
US consumer sentiment on Friday coming in below the 47.5 forecast, or inflation expectations falling from 4.6%, which would make Fed rises less likely and weaken the dollar.
watch: On Friday the University of Michigan publishes US consumer sentiment at 18:00 Dubai, forecast at 47.5 after 47.8, together with inflation expectations, previously 4.6%. A lower figure on either would help someone selling pounds for dirhams.

feed.title: The dollar has weakened after the President ruled out striking Iran before the midterms
feed.text: President Trump wrote on Truth Social that the United States will not attack Iran at any time before the midterm elections on 3 November and that productive discussions with Tehran are under way, in a post reported shortly before 21:00 Dubai. Brent crude eased from about $105.90 (about £80) a barrel to about $104 (about £79) and the US ten-year yield fell to about 5.24%, its lowest since Monday, NBC News and Trading Economics reported; cheaper oil eases US inflation worries and lower US yields draw less money into the dollar, which means more dirhams per pound. GBP/USD rose from 1.3206 at 20:30 Dubai to 1.3214 by 21:00, then from 1.3216 at 21:04 to 1.3235 at 21:19, and stood near 1.3231 at 21:38; the euro rose in step, from 1.1193 to 1.1213, so this was the dollar weakening and nothing in the UK. A sale of 30-year US bonds at 21:00 Dubai drew ordinary demand and gave no push either way.

feed.title: The dollar has taken back its late-afternoon dip as oil and US yields climbed again
feed.text: Brent crude rose to about $105.50 (about £80) a barrel, up more than 5% on the day, and the US ten-year yield went back up to about 5.3% after slipping to 5.28%, AFP and Trading Economics reported; an analyst quoted by AFP said shares were falling because oil was rising sharply and bond yields were returning to Wednesday's peak. Dearer oil adds to US inflation worries and higher US yields draw money into the dollar, which means fewer dirhams per pound. GBP/USD fell from 1.3246 at 18:37 Dubai to 1.3227 by 19:00 and 1.3211 by 19:38, giving back almost all of the rise of the hour before, and the euro fell in step, from 1.1222 to 1.1193, while the pound was flat against the euro, so this was the dollar recovering and nothing in the UK. No single headline is timed to the fall.

feed.title: The dollar has eased as US bond yields came off their high
feed.text: The US ten-year yield slipped back to about 5.28% after touching 5.35% earlier on Thursday, its highest since 2002, Trading Economics reported, and lower US yields draw less money into the dollar, which means more dirhams per pound. GBP/USD rose from 1.3204 at 16:40 Dubai to 1.3246 at 18:37, with the sharpest part from 1.3223 at 18:22 to 1.3246 fifteen minutes later, and the euro rose in step, from 1.1186 to 1.1219, while the pound was flat against the euro, so this was the dollar weakening and nothing in the UK. No source names a cause for those fifteen minutes; Iran's foreign minister had said earlier in the afternoon that talks through mediators continue and that Tehran will answer the US within days, yet Brent crude was still near $104.90 (about £79) a barrel, up more than 4% on the day.

feed.title: US jobless claims came in a little below forecast and the rate barely moved
feed.text: New claims for unemployment benefit in the week to 3 October were 197,000 against 200,000 expected, and the week before was revised up from 197,000 to 199,000, the Labor Department said. A job market that firm keeps another Fed rise in view, which supports the dollar and means fewer dirhams per pound, but the gap to the forecast was small. GBP/USD slipped from 1.3211 just before the figure at 16:30 Dubai to 1.3206 within the minute, was back at 1.3211 two minutes later and stood near 1.3205 by 16:39, and the euro eased alongside it, from 1.1195 to 1.1188.

feed.title: The Bank of England Governor gave no signal on rates
feed.text: Andrew Bailey's speech in Istanbul was about financial resilience in a world of repeated shocks; he spoke of an unwavering commitment to returning inflation to target but said nothing on Bank Rate or the decision on 5 November, and a speech has no forecast to compare against. With no new signal on UK rates there was nothing to move the pound, and GBP/USD was 1.3204 at the scheduled start at 16:15 Dubai and 1.3205 five minutes later. The rate had already risen from 1.3192 at 16:00 Dubai to 1.3205 by 16:07, before he spoke, and the euro rose in the same minutes, from 1.1176 to 1.1185, so that was the dollar easing and no source names a cause for it.

feed.title: The dollar has firmed after a Fed governor backed more rate rises
feed.text: Fed Governor Waller said in Istanbul that, if the figures keep coming in as expected, he anticipates additional rises to bring inflation back to 2% sooner, that they need not come at consecutive meetings, and that the job market was solid and stable in September; a speech has no forecast to compare against. Talk of more Fed rises lifts US yields and the dollar, which means fewer dirhams per pound. GBP/USD fell from 1.3203 just before the text came out at 12:30 Dubai to 1.3190 by 12:39, and the euro fell alongside it, from 1.1197 to 1.1186, so this was the dollar gaining and not anything in the UK.

feed.title: The dollar firmed briefly as Europe opened
feed.text: GBP/USD slipped from 1.3200 at 10:45 Dubai to a low of 1.3185 at 11:06, just after European trading began, then recovered to 1.3205 by 11:24 and settled near 1.3198. The euro fell and recovered against the dollar in the same minutes while the pound was flat against the euro, so this was a move in the dollar and not in sterling. No source names a cause for it; the backdrop is Brent crude above $103 (about £78) a barrel, a two-week high, after reports that the White House asked the Pentagon for options to strike Iran, and dearer oil tends to lift the dollar.

feed.title: Sterling has been steady overnight after the Fed minutes
feed.text: GBP/USD has stayed between 1.3204 and 1.3220 since the Fed minutes, touching the low at 05:00 Dubai and the high at 06:15, and stood near 1.3209 at 07:38 Dubai. The dollar index held above 102, near its strongest since spring 2025, because the minutes showed most Fed policymakers expecting another rate rise by the end of the year, Trading Economics reported, and a firm dollar means fewer dirhams per pound. No scheduled figure came out overnight, and the euro was just as steady, between 1.1194 and 1.1210.

feed.title: Oil has risen on a report of US strike options against Iran
feed.text: The Atlantic reported that the White House has asked the Pentagon to prepare options for strikes on Iran that could be carried out before the US midterm elections on 3 November, and a White House official said only that the President has all options available, the Jerusalem Post reported. Brent stood near $102.10 (about £77) a barrel early on Thursday, with a tropical storm also shutting in more than 510,000 barrels a day of output in the Gulf of Mexico, Trading Economics reported. Dearer oil and Gulf tension add to US inflation worries and tend to lift the dollar, which means fewer dirhams per pound, but GBP/USD has not moved outside its overnight range of 1.3204 to 1.3220, so the effect on the rate so far is small.

feed.title: The Fed minutes have barely moved the rate
feed.text: The minutes of the Fed's meeting of 15 and 16 September record that all participants supported the rise to a range of 3.75% to 4%, and that most thought another rise would likely be appropriate by the end of the year, while stressing that later decisions depend on the figures that come in; they carry no forecast to compare against. Talk of a further rise would normally lift the dollar and mean fewer dirhams per pound, but the market already put the chance of a rise by December at about 84.5%, and the meeting came before the soft September jobs figures. GBP/USD was 1.3215 at the release at 22:00 Dubai, dipped to 1.3211, touched 1.3219 at 22:05 and was back near 1.3215 by 22:40, and the euro was just as steady, from 1.1198 to 1.1195.

feed.title: The President's announcement has not moved the rate
feed.text: The White House announcement at 21:00 Dubai was billed in advance as being about automatic enrolment of children in the government's savings accounts, which carry a one-off $1,000 (about £760) for those born from 2025 to 2028, and the reports read before it named nothing on interest rates, trade or the Gulf. A domestic savings scheme gives traders no reason to reprice the dollar or the pound, and GBP/USD was 1.3210 at the start, touched 1.3216 twenty minutes later and was back at 1.3210 by 21:35 Dubai. The Fed minutes at 22:00 Dubai remain the test of the evening.

feed.title: The dollar has reached its highest since March 2025
feed.text: The dollar index has risen about 0.6% on Wednesday to above 102.4, its highest level since March 2025, as the US ten-year yield climbed about five basis points to 5.34%, a level last seen in 2002, and Brent crude held near $101.70 (about £77), Trading Economics reported. Dearer oil adds to US inflation worries and higher US yields draw money into the dollar, which means fewer dirhams per pound. GBP/USD slid steadily from 1.3227 at 13:39 Dubai to a low of 1.3192 at 16:27 and stood near 1.3197 at 16:39; the euro fell by a similar amount, from 1.1187 to 1.1170, so this is the dollar gaining rather than anything in the UK, and no scheduled figure came out and no source names a single trigger.

feed.title: The dollar has strengthened ahead of the Fed minutes
feed.text: The dollar has risen against every major currency on Wednesday morning, with the dollar index up about 0.45% near 102.3, as the US ten-year yield held near 5.33% and Brent crude stayed above $101 (about £77) after further Iranian attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, Trading Economics reported. Higher US yields and dearer oil tend to lift the dollar, and the euro fell furthest, from 1.1235 to 1.1188, under the added weight of doubts over France's budget and the election called in Spain. GBP/USD slipped from 1.3251 to 1.3226 between 07:45 and 13:30 Dubai, with the sharpest fall, from 1.3245 to 1.3229, in the quarter of an hour before 12:00 Dubai; no scheduled figure came out at that time and no source names a single trigger for it.

feed.title: Sterling has held most of Tuesday's gain overnight
feed.text: GBP/USD peaked at 1.3284 at 19:30 Dubai on Tuesday, stayed between 1.3261 and 1.3284 through the US session, then eased in Asian trading to a low of 1.3248 at 06:15 Dubai and stood near 1.3252 at 07:38. The dollar index fell 0.27% on Tuesday and was steady at 101.94 early on Wednesday, Reuters reported, as stress in European bond markets eased and traders judged that the recent soft US inflation and jobs figures leave the Fed in less of a hurry to raise rates. A weaker dollar means more dirhams per pound; the small slip since midnight is the dollar recovering a little, since the euro fell by a similar amount, from 1.1259 to 1.1232, and no scheduled figure came out.

feed.title: Oil has risen back above $101 on tanker attacks
feed.text: Brent rose about 1% to near $101.50 (about £77) a barrel early on Wednesday, its second rise in a row, after Iran stepped up attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, with nine incidents reported this month, and a Saudi-led coalition intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile, Trading Economics reported. Dearer oil adds to US inflation worries and tends to lift the dollar, which means fewer dirhams per pound. Oil is still lower for the week because Gulf exports are recovering, and GBP/USD has eased only from 1.3270 at 02:00 Dubai to about 1.3252, so the effect so far is small.

feed.title: The dollar has weakened as oil falls again
feed.text: Brent fell about 2% to near $98.30 (about £74) a barrel, its third fall in a row, as Saudi Arabia reported 5.8 million barrels flowing through its East-West Pipeline and Middle East exports recover, Trading Economics reported, and the dollar index slipped below 102 to about 101.87. Cheaper oil eases US inflation worries and the case for Fed rises, which weakens the dollar and means more dirhams per pound. GBP/USD rose from 1.3211 at 11:00 Dubai, as London opened, to 1.3243 at 13:00; the euro rose by a similar 0.3% and the pound was unchanged against the euro, so nothing in the UK lies behind it.

feed.title: Sterling has climbed above 1.3260 with no named cause
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from 1.3246 at 15:12 Dubai to 1.3266 at 15:30, above the range of 1.3180 to 1.3250 it had kept since Friday, and stood near 1.3262 at 15:39. The euro rose by a similar 0.15% against the dollar in those minutes and the pound was unchanged against the euro, so this is the dollar giving more ground rather than anything in the UK. No source names an event for those minutes, and no scheduled figure came out; BBH, quoted by FXStreet at 15:15 Dubai, said the dollar had trimmed its recent gains while futures still price a full Fed rise in December.

feed.title: Sterling has held just above 1.32 overnight
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from 1.3200 at 18:40 Dubai on Monday to 1.3224 by 19:00, then stayed between 1.3200 and 1.3227 through the US session and Tuesday's Asian trading, and stood near 1.3217 at 07:38 Dubai. The dollar index is steady near 102.16, just under Monday's 18-month high, and the euro is still near 1.1220, its weakest since May 2025, Reuters reported. No scheduled figure came out overnight, so the forces of Monday are unchanged: high US yields and the euro's troubles hold the dollar up, which means fewer dirhams per pound, while weak US jobs figures and cheaper oil hold it back.

feed.title: Oil has slipped as Gulf exports recover
feed.text: Brent closed Monday near $100.70 (about £76) a barrel and US crude fell to about $88.50 (about £67) early on Tuesday, Trading Economics and FXStreet reported, citing the G7 release and a JPMorgan estimate that Middle East crude shipments are back to about 98% of their pre-war level. Cheaper oil eases US inflation worries and tends to weaken the dollar, which would mean more dirhams per pound. Against that, the Houthis claimed three further missile and drone operations against airports, an oil facility and military sites in Saudi Arabia, and GBP/USD has barely moved, so the two have so far cancelled out.

feed.title: The US services survey was slightly soft, but prices rose
feed.text: The ISM services index for September came in at 54.9 against 55.1 forecast and 55.4 in August, Trading Economics reported, while its measure of prices paid rose to 74.0 from 72.6, the highest since July 2022, and its employment measure returned to growth at 50.1 from 47.8. A softer headline makes Fed rises a little less likely, which weakens the dollar, but faster price rises and firmer hiring point the other way, so the two largely cancelled out. GBP/USD rose from 1.3195 just before the release at 18:00 Dubai to 1.3202 four minutes later, touched 1.3205 at 18:12 and 1.3207 at 18:32, and stood near 1.3200 at 18:38.

feed.title: The dollar has strengthened as the euro hits a 17-month low
feed.text: Spain's prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, called a snap election today after Congress rejected his housing measures, which added to the worries over France's budget and took the euro to its weakest against the dollar since May 2025, Trading Economics and FXStreet reported. Money leaving the euro lifts the dollar against every currency, the pound included, which means fewer dirhams per pound. GBP/USD slid steadily from 1.3221 at 16:35 Dubai to 1.3192 at 17:38, with a low of 1.3191, while the euro fell by a similar 0.2% against the dollar and the pound was little changed against the euro, so nothing in the UK lies behind it; the US services survey follows at 18:00 Dubai.

feed.title: The dollar has firmed again as the euro slips
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from 1.3230 at 13:38 Dubai to 1.3216 at 13:45 and has since held between about 1.3218 and 1.3225. The euro fell by the same 0.1% against the dollar in those minutes and the pound was unchanged against the euro, so this is the dollar strengthening, which means fewer dirhams per pound, and nothing in the UK. No source names a single event for those minutes; FXStreet, writing at 14:37 Dubai, put the dollar's strength down to heavy selling of the euro over France's budget, high long-term US yields and geopolitical tension, and Trading Economics added political uncertainty in Spain.

feed.title: The dollar has eased back from its morning high
feed.text: FXStreet put the dollar index near 102.53, a new high for the year, at about 10:00 Dubai, and Trading Economics showed it near 102.19 later in the morning, as London and Europe opened. Trading Economics also reported Brent slipping towards $101 (about £76) a barrel earlier in the session on signs of rising supply, which eases the pull of the dollar. GBP/USD has climbed steadily from about 1.3192 at 08:30 Dubai to about 1.3230 at 12:35 Dubai, recovering most of the early fall; the euro rose by about the same 0.3% over those hours, so this is the dollar giving ground, and no source names a single event for it.

feed.title: The dollar has strengthened in Asian trading
feed.text: FXStreet reported the dollar index above 102.20 just before 07:00 Dubai, citing higher US Treasury yields, the conflicts in the Middle East, worries about France's budget and remarks from the Fed's Lorie Logan that rates need to rise by at least a further 50 basis points. Money moving into the dollar for safety and for yield means fewer dirhams per pound. GBP/USD fell from 1.3233 at 06:00 Dubai to 1.3217 at 06:42 and a low of 1.3188 at 07:08, then recovered to about 1.3201 by 07:38; no source names a single event for the sharpest minutes. The euro fell further than the pound, about 0.5% against 0.3%, which points to the dollar and the euro, not to anything in the UK.
